data.narrative:
Epoch Biodesign is a Series A biotech company founded by Jacob Nathan that has raised $40M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given data constraints. Stage-progression analysis uses the $40M total raised as a proxy for current post-money valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding an implied $80M valuation. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because Epoch's revenue is not on file—standard practice for private biotech at this stage. Peer-median analysis failed due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables (the broader Biotech & Health peer set of 7 targets lacks the minimum 3 tight-filter matches needed to anchor reliably).

The single-method result supports a valuation range of $68M to $92M, with a median of $80M. This range reflects typical expansion between Series A and subsequent funding rounds but carries material uncertainty given reliance on one method and the absence of revenue-based or peer multiple validation. Key uncertainties include technology maturity, clinical or preclinical stage, cash burn trajectory, and competitive positioning relative to the identified peer set.
